req_desc:
Pre-match notice panel
On first load a modal notice panel offers Calm effects or Enter before anything else is interactive, and the choice persists so the panel does not return.

Title screen
The title screen shows the Holdfast pixel wordmark, the start-a-room bar, two title menu link rows and the build and tick stamp, and each control opens its screen.

Callsign sessions
A player starts a session with a callsign, and the seeded studio key grants the founder role, as specified in API.

Service status banner
The server reports each dependency as up or down, and every screen shows a truthful banner while one is down and clears it after recovery, within the delays in Server boundary.

Room creation
A signed-in player creates a siege or convoy room with a unique short code and becomes its host, and a founder's room is linked to a live night of the same mode.

Joining by code
A player joins a lobby by code into the lowest free seat, a repeated join returns the same seat, and full, mid-match and unknown rooms are refused with their published errors.

Invite expiry edge
A room's invite accepts new joins strictly before its expiry instant and refuses them from that instant on.

Ready-up and start
Seated players toggle ready in the lobby, and only the host can start, only when every seated player is ready, which begins the server countdown.

Lobby to first wave
In the browser a player starts a room, a second player joins by code, both ready up, the host starts, and both screens move from lobby through countdown to wave 1.

Server-moved players
Players send movement intents with sequence numbers, the server moves them at the published speed and never into solid blocks, and stale sequence numbers are ignored.

Fire interval and reload
A shot faster than the fire interval, during a reload, or with an empty magazine is rejected with its published reason and changes no ammo, and a reload refills from reserve after the reload duration.

Shot resolution
The server resolves each accepted shot along the aim angle, so it hits the first enemy or barrel in range unless a solid block is in the way, and applies the published damage.

Room state and stream
The room state reports phase, every remaining-milliseconds timer, players, enemies, barrels, grenades, shop prices and recent events, both on request and as a stream at the server tick rate.

Combat HUD
In the browser the HUD shows the server's health, ammo, grenades, credits, wave and timers, and they change when the player fires, reloads and kills an enemy.

Report ids apply once
Each shot, reload, grenade or revive report id changes the game at most once, and a replay returns the stored outcome.

Report conflicts and races
A reused report id with a different body is refused as a conflict, and identical reports sent at the same moment are applied exactly once with identical responses.

Reconnect replay
In the browser a player who loses the connection mid-wave sees the reconnecting notice, regains the seat, and after replaying buffered reports sees ammo, credits and score counted once.

Wave progression
A siege runs three waves, each followed by a timed intermission, then a boss wave, with the spawns, bonuses and timings in Business rules and Seed data.

Enemy behaviour
Enemies move through patrol, detect, pursue, attack and dead under the published ranges, speeds and damage.

Grenade splash
A grenade detonates when its server fuse ends and damages enemies and barrels with the published falloff by distance, except where a solid block is in the way.

Barrel chain reactions
A barrel brought to zero health explodes once, and chained explosions resolve in the published order within the same tick, each one logged.

Match history
A finished match is stored with its result and each player's score, kills and credits earned, and History lists matches newest first across restarts.

Siege run to debrief
In the browser a squad that clears the boss wave sees the Debrief panel with the server's results and finds the match in History.

Downed and revive window
A player at zero health is downed with a revive window, and a nearby teammate's revive succeeds only while the window has time left.

Out, respawn and defeat
A downed player whose window runs out is out until the next intermission, and the match ends in defeat when no player is up.

Reviving a teammate
In the browser a player sees a downed teammate's revive window, moves close and revives them, and both screens show the teammate up again.

Paired credit ledger
Every credit movement writes two opposite entries, each balance equals the sum of its entries, and a match's entries sum to zero.

Shop hours and purchases
Purchases succeed only during an intermission, at the price in effect at the server moment of purchase, and are idempotent by purchase id.

Ammo station drawer
In the browser the ammo station drawer opens during an intermission, buys by keyboard or pointer, updates credits and ammo, and closes when the next wave starts.

Seat leases and reconnect grace
A seat with no traffic for the lease time becomes disconnected and is held for the reconnect grace, which a returning player meets strictly before it runs out.

Host migration
When the host disconnects or leaves, hosting passes at once to the connected player in the lowest seat, and the change is logged.

Dropped host takeover
In the browser, when the host drops, the next player sees that they are now host and can use the host-only controls.

Convoy laps and checkpoints
Convoy racers pass checkpoints only in order, and the server times each lap on its own clock for three laps.

Pose speed check
A pose that moves farther than top speed allows for the server time elapsed is rejected and leaves the vehicle unchanged.

Wreck and reset
A pose inside a solid block or outside the map wrecks the vehicle, and after the reset delay it is placed at its last passed checkpoint facing the next one.

Lap board
Completed laps are stored, and the Lap board lists each racer's best lap, fastest first, across restarts.

Driving a convoy lap
In the browser a racer drives one full lap and sees the checkpoint counter, the server lap time, any wreck reset and the new entry on the Lap board.

Weekly nights in the studio zone
The founder schedules a weekly series as a weekday and local wall time in the studio zone, and each night's date is its studio-local date.

Skipped and repeated hours
A night whose local time falls in a skipped or repeated hour follows the published rule, and every other week keeps its wall-clock time across daylight-saving changes.

Night status from the server clock
Each night's status and the time until it changes come from the server clock, and the browser shows them even when the device clock is wrong.

Nights screen in two zones
In the browser the Nights list groups nights by studio date and shows each start in studio time and the viewer's time, and the founder schedules a series from it.

Effective-dated prices
The founder schedules ammo-station price changes at a studio-local instant, a purchase from that instant on pays the new price, and past purchases keep the price they paid.

Scheduling a price change
In the browser the founder schedules a price change, sees it pending with a countdown, removes a pending one, and cannot remove one in effect.

Sign-up window edges
Sign-ups are accepted from the opening instant and strictly before the closing instant, up to the night's capacity, with exactly the free seats won under contention.

One sign-up per email
A repeated sign-up for the same night with the same email returns the existing sign-up and sends no second email.

Confirmation and reminder emails
Each sign-up gets one confirmation and one reminder email that print the night in studio time and the viewer's time.

Mail outage queue
While mail is down, sign-ups still succeed with the email queued, and each queued email is sent exactly once after mail returns, without a restart.

Phone sign-up
On a phone viewport a spectator opens Nights, signs up for a night, and sees the confirmation copy and the deadline timer from the server.

Pause menu sections
The pause menu and Settings show Game, Controls, Audio and Comfort sections, and a collapsed section is hidden, unfocusable and absent from the accessibility tree.

Key remapping
Players remap every action to a key, conflicts are refused with the published message, and bindings persist in their settings.

Keyboard-complete dialogs
Every dialog and drawer traps Tab and Shift+Tab, closes on Escape, returns focus to its opener, and game keys work whichever HUD control has focus.

Tuning comfort and controls
In the browser a player opens the pause menu by keyboard, remaps Fire, turns on Reduce effects, resumes, and finds both choices kept after a reload.

Fuse Clock
Every server-decided timer shows as a Fuse Clock numeral that follows the server's remaining milliseconds, re-flows to each snapshot, resolves to its outcome at zero, and appears in the Timers list.

Reduced effects
Under reduced motion or Reduce effects, the stage drift, shake, camera bob, numeral rolls and splits stop, and every value, outcome and announcement stays.

Touch controls
On touch devices the HUD shows move and aim sticks and Fire, Reload, Grenade and Pause buttons that drive the same server actions as the keyboard.

Responsive layers
Every screen fits 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 as fixed layers over the stage, with no document scroll or horizontal overflow and with tap targets of at least 44 px.

Siege field stage
A live 3D block-field stage sits behind every screen, with the published idle motion, input response, reduced-motion stillness and a still fallback without WebGL.

Server boundary
The server serves same-origin only, enforces the body-size and content-type limits, never serves source or credentials, and boots and recovers with dependencies down.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Visual design
Screens carry the dark teal tactical-terminal look with the pixel display face, the condensed body face, smoked-glass panels and mint kept for primary actions.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and the app runs only through it.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its licence, where shipped packages are the Go modules the program imports plus the frontend production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), and the fonts.
Every shipped package and font uses MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0, Zlib, CC0-1.0, Unlicense or OFL-1.1, and nothing GPL, LGPL, AGPL or SSPL ships.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres, Valkey and Mailpit; there is no SQLite, embedded database, or file used as a database.
The seed records (studio, studio key, prices, series and maps) match Seed data exactly and are not altered by migrations or code.
go.sum and the frontend lockfile are committed, and the build works offline from them after install.
Fonts are Pixelify Sans and Chakra Petch, loaded from Google Fonts or vendored OFL files, and no art, audio, models or text comes from another game or website.
